metadata.title: For Huge Powers, Keep Only the Last Digit
metadata.description: Master cyclic unit-digit patterns, last-two/last-three digit reasoning, and power expressions modulo 10 or 100.

content.text: The units digit of a power repeats in a short cycle. For bases ending in 3, the cycle is 3,9,7,1; for 7 it is 7,9,3,1; for 4 it alternates 4,6.
Reduce exponents by the cycle length. For a product, discard every digit except the units digit. For last-two-digit questions, move to modulo 100 before doing anything large.
A useful shortcut is to look for forced endings: a factor ending in 5 combined with an even factor forces a product ending in 0.
Now solve several products at once.
Finish with a difference of two large powers.
Great. Huge exponents no longer need huge calculations.
